messages:
maria_support: FYI — incoming customer request from ACME via support ticket #45321. They want streaming chat + function/tool calling events + a final structured JSON envelope for classifications. Their note: "we need partial tool-call results as they stream, and a strict schema for the final object so downstream systems can parse reliably."

sam_support: copy of ticket excerpt pasted below: 
> Customer says some responses are large; they want toolcalls to stream so UI can show progress and final structured metadata for downstream analytics. Attaching sample output they currently expect.

maria_support: link to ticket + logs: https://support.redwood.ai/t/45321 — customer included a couple of example prompts and a failing output snippet.

alex_engineer: quick questions: what do they mean by "partial tool-call results" — are these separate event frames (like tool_call_start, tool_call_chunk, tool_call_end) or just tokens that include tool payloads? Also, expected concurrency and latency SLO?

maria_support: they asked for event frames — sample from customer: 
```
{
  "event":"tool_call_start",
  "name":"search",
  "meta":{ "query":"enterprise billing" }
}
...streaming chunks...
{
  "event":"tool_call_end",
  "result_summary":"3 hits"
}
{
  "event":"final_structured",
  "schema_version":"1.0",
  "payload":{ "intent":"billing_issue","case_id":"ACME-998" }
}
```

jason_product: prioritization ask: is this blocking a close or churn risk? Kai / sales — can you weigh in on ARR impact?

kai_sales: ACME is ~$120k ARR and evaluating Dedicated for next quarter. If streaming fncall + schema is a hard requirement it's high priority for their deal. Not a showstopper for everyone though.

alex_engineer: from an implementation POV: we already stream token-level events for chat. Adding explicit event frames for function/tool lifecycle and a final structured envelope is doable but has compatibility surface: SDKs (JS/Python), our streaming framing protocol, and proxies/load balancers. Also need to define an extensible event model.

jason_product: proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- schema for event frames (tool_call_start, tool_call_chunk, tool_call_end, final_structured) documented
- fallback: non-streaming clients receive consolidated single response (backcompat)
- SDK examples for JS/Python + console sample
- end-to-end test + perf budget (p50 token latency change < 10%)
- canary rollout plan + monitoring and rollback

maria_support: customer also requested structured envelope validation — they want 422-like errors when final payload doesn't match customer schema. They want this enforced server-side.

alex_engineer: server-side validation is extra work but reasonable as an opt-in feature (customer supplies schema or picks from named schema). Implementation plan: spike (2 weeks) to propose wire format and SDK changes; then a phased PR for runtime + validation + docs.

jason_product: prioritization: tentatively P1 for sales-influenced backlog (ACME deal), but P2 for general roadmap unless we see more customers. Decision: run spike now, then reassess for full implementation.

maria_support: I'll gather 3 more customer examples (different industries) and ask them to confirm allowed schema fields. ETA 3 business days.

alex_engineer: tentative timeline if spike greenlights:
- 2w spike -> design + wire format + perf experiments
- 4w implementation (runtime + validation)
- 1w SDK updates + docs
- 1w canary + rollouts = ~8w from greenlight to GA
(we'll tighten after spike)

jason_product: rollout plan notes: canary at 10% tenants, synthetic load tests & regression on p99 latency, automatic rollback if error rate > 1% or p50 latency regress > 20%. Also add a migration guide for customers moving from token-only streams.

sam_support: action items: 
- maria_support: collect sample payloads + confirm schema acceptance (3 days)
- alex_engineer: start spike ticket and post design doc stub (assign in 2 days)
- jason_product: prepare acceptance criteria card and link to sales notes
- kai_sales: sync w/ACME on timeline and set expectation that canary may take a few weeks

deploybot: new ticket created: INF-8703 (spike) by alex_engineer — https://go.redwood.ai/INF-8703

maria_support: +1. tagging @alex_engineer here so we can pair on test vectors.

alex_engineer: noted. I'll add an example streaming frame spec in the spike doc. early sketch: 
```
// Server-sent event style frames (outline)
data: {"type":"token","text":"hello"}
data: {"type":"tool_call_start","name":"search","meta":{...}}
data: {"type":"tool_call_chunk","chunk":"..."}
data: {"type":"tool_call_end","summary":{...}}
data: {"type":"final_structured","schema_version":"1.0","payload":{...}}
[data: DONE]
```

jason_product: good. keep UX simple for customers: opt-in flag on the API (stream_events=true) and a named schema param (schema=acme_billing_v1).

kai_sales: once spike is green, I'll ask ACME to join early access for Dedicated if needed.

maria_support: logging note: include per-event trace_id so customer can reconcile logs with their pipeline.

alex_engineer: yep will include trace_id and sequence numbers in spec.

jason_product: ok team — thanks. We'll reconvene after spike update. Marking this thread as triaged. :thumbsup:
